# TurboLapper workspace

Loaded into every agent session started in the workspace root (`workspace_root` in
`instantiation/turbolapper.answers.yaml`, by default `~/Documents/repos`)
(`CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` there are symlinks to this file). Two macOS apps for
on-device data analysis, one fork relationship. Other sibling directories under this
workspace root are unrelated projects — ignore them.

| Repo | What it is |
|---|---|
| `turbolapper-mac` | The **superset** app (remote: `turbolapper-super-mac`). Local Data Connector: drag in a data file, auto-model it with an LLM, expose it to Claude Desktop / any MCP client as typed queryable views. GUI (SwiftUI) + MCP server (`TurbolapperMCP`) + CLI (`tlapctl`). Multi-provider, including an embedded on-device model. |
| `turbolapper-fm-mac` | The **Apple Foundation Models edition**, a true fork of the superset. Single job: on-device report builder using Apple Intelligence. Deliberately has no model picker and no connector — absent, not hidden (`product-specs/apple-fm-native.md`). |

## The cross-repo contract: a fork, not a library

The repos share a root commit and an identical skeleton (`App/`, `engine/` Swift
package, `extension/`, `fastlane/`, `project.yml`). There is **no shared package
dependency between them** — code moves by porting, not by import. That means:

- A fix in shared-skeleton code (`engine/`, build scripts, `project.yml`
  conventions) in one repo is a **candidate port** to the other. Say so explicitly
  when touching such code; use `workspace_search` to check whether the same code
  exists on the other side before assuming.
- The fm edition **removes** capability on purpose. Never "fix" it by
  reintroducing model pickers, connectors, or provider plumbing from the superset.
  When in doubt, `product-specs/apple-fm-native.md` is the promise.
- Product direction lives in each repo's `product-specs/` (fm edition:
  `product-specs/HANDOFF.md` is the front door; mockups are the source of truth
  for feel).

## Which session, which skill

**Claude Code resolves skills, commands and `.mcp.json` from the session's own
project root.** It does not look into subdirectories. So the harness commands and
a repo's own skills never appear together by default — **cwd is the switch**, and
it is not configurable.

| Session opened at | Has |
|---|---|
| **this workspace root** | `/delegate`, `/fix-issue`, `/harness-init`, `/review-pr`; the `offload` + `delegate` MCP tools |
| **a product repo root** | that repo's `.claude/skills/`: `/build-out`, `/dev-loop`, `/release`, `/ship-testflight`, `/setup-release-secrets`. `turbolapper-fm-mac` also carries its own `.mcp.json`, so the offload tools come along; `turbolapper-mac` does not yet (candidate port) |

Rule of thumb: **cross-repo work → the workspace root. Building or shipping one
repo → that repo's root.** To run `/build-out`, open Claude Code *in the repo* and
state the merge scope in your own words — the skill's §0 gate will not merge
without it, and no flag grants it.

Both repos define the **same five skill names**, already diverged. Which repo you
opened decides which policy you get; that is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

Unattended, `agent-harness/bin/issue-watch` runs a repo's own poll script on a
launchd interval (it `cd`s into the repo first — otherwise the tick dies on
`Unknown command: /dev-loop`). `/build-out` is excluded from that path on purpose:
it merges, and it takes its scope from a human who is present.

## Build & test (details in each repo's CLAUDE.md — read it before building)

- Engine: `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer sh -c 'cd engine && swift build && swift test'`
- App: `./run-app.sh` (xcodegen → xcodebuild → launch). **Only** the `xcodebuild`
  path works for the app — `swift run` misses `default.metallib` and MLX crashes at
  runtime. Both repos document this identically; respect it.
- Requires macOS 26 / Xcode 26 (Swift 6.2).

## Python upstream

The original Turbolapper web app (public-data warehouse + semantic SQL) lives at
`ideas/Eric/` in this workspace root. It is context, not a build dependency.

## Conventions

- Per-repo conventions, worktree rules, and release steps live in each repo's own
  `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` — this file never duplicates them.
- Cross-repo work: state the plan per repo before editing, keep the fork symmetric
  where the skeleton is shared, and open separate PRs per repo.
